records.question: In a laboratory vacuum chamber where all air is evacuated, a 10-gram feather and a 5-kilogram iron bowling ball are released simultaneously from the exact same height. Which one hits the floor first?
records.final_answer: In a vacuum, air resistance is zero. Since gravitational acceleration (g) is independent of mass, both objects hit the floor at the exact same time.
completed_facts: In a true vacuum, there is no air resistance acting on objects falling towards Earth.
The only force acting on both the feather and the iron ball during their fall is gravity.
On Earth, the gravitational acceleration near the surface is approximately 9.8 meters per second squared.

records.question: Can a healthy human being survive and breathe normally underwater at 50 meters depth by simply using a 50-meter-long ordinary hollow snorkel tube extending to the surface?
records.final_answer: At 50 meters depth, water pressure is approximately 6 atmospheres. Human respiratory muscles cannot overcome this pressure differential to inhale surface air through a snorkel; the human will suffer fatal barotrauma.
completed_facts: Hydrostatic pressure increases with depth in water.
The volume of a gas decreases as its pressure increases.
Human lungs can expand up to about three times their resting size.

completed_facts: The moon has no atmosphere to slow down falling objects.

completed_facts: Stainless steel conducts heat well and can overheat quickly when exposed to high temperatures for extended periods.

records.question: If someone habitually cracks the knuckles of their fingers daily for fifty years, what physical condition do controlled clinical trials show they inevitably develop in those joints?

completed_facts: Controlled clinical trials have shown that habitual cracking of knuckles can lead to joint problems over time.
